original_target.title: A spectral gap for almost every pair of quantum gates

full_original_statement:
Let $`G=\mathrm{SU}(2)=\{U\in\mathbb C^{2\times2}:U^*U=I,\det U=1\}`$, with Haar probability measure $`\mu`$. For $`a,b\in G`$, define the lazy averaging operator on $`L^2(G,\mu)`$ by

```math
P_{a,b}f(g)=\frac12 f(g)+\frac18\bigl(f(ag)+f(a^{-1}g)+f(bg)+f(b^{-1}g)\bigr).
```

Is it true that for $`(\mu\otimes\mu)`$-almost every pair $`(a,b)`$ there exists $`\delta(a,b)>0`$ such that

```math
\|P_{a,b}f\|_2\le(1-\delta(a,b))\|f\|_2
\quad\text{whenever }f\in L^2(G,\mu),\quad\int_G f\,d\mu=0?
```

The gap may depend on the chosen pair; no positive bound uniform over all pairs is requested.

sources.scope_comparison: The target asks whether Haar-almost every fixed pair has a pair-dependent L2 gap for its symmetric lazy finite-support walk. Current October19v2actualTheorem1.1 still proves only zero or full measure without choosing the alternative;algebraic examples have zero Haar measure. Baer–Haah's2026constant-gap Theorem1.3 samples fresh rotation angles or fresh local Haar gates at each step, rather than fixing two Haar generators. Thus neither resolves the exact almost-everywhere pair target. No full matching announcement was found.
